examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
DP states must retain sufficient information for future choices, not the full history. Define a recurrence, base cases and an evaluation order following dependencies. Complexity is states times transitions per state. Recovering the chosen solution can require predecessor information beyond the optimum value. In one-dimensional 0/1 knapsack, descending capacities prevent reusing an item; ascending capacities instead permit repetition.

**Key relationship:** 0/1 knapsack: DP[i,w]=max(DP[i−1,w], valueᵢ+DP[i−1,w−weightᵢ]) when weightᵢ≤w

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Define state semantics.
2. Derive transitions and bases.
3. Count states and ensure dependency-safe order.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Define a sufficient state, recurrence, base cases and dependency-respecting evaluation order. Count states times transition cost. Row-major and diagonal orders can both be correct but have different overhead. Recovering an actual solution may require predecessor pointers in addition to optimum values.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
0/1 knapsack capacity is 5; items (weight,value) are (2,3),(3,4),(4,5). What is the optimum value?

**Answer: 7.** The first two items together use weight 5 and give value 7. The weight-4 item gives 5 and cannot combine with another. Thus the optimum is 7.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
For one-dimensional 0/1 knapsack, iterate capacities downward; upward iteration can reuse the same item and instead solve an unbounded variant.

A state missing a necessary constraint can combine incompatible partial solutions and produce a wrong answer.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

One-dimensional 0/1 knapsack capacities are usually iterated:

- **A.** Upward to reuse the item
- **B.** Downward to avoid item reuse
- **C.** In any order always
- **D.** Only at capacity zero

**Answer: B.** Descending order ensures each transition reads the previous item's state rather than a value already updated with the same item.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** State meaning should be explicit
- **B.** Optimal substructure alone guarantees a linear-time DP
- **C.** Transition cost contributes to runtime
- **D.** Solution reconstruction may need predecessor data

**Answer: A, C, D.** State count and transitions may be large despite optimal substructure, so B is false.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

0/1 knapsack capacity 6, items (weight,value)=(2,4),(3,5),(4,7). Maximum value?



**Answer: 11.** Items of weights 2 and 4 fit exactly and give 4+7=11. Other feasible combinations give at most 9.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2024 CS2 · Q35 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/dynamic-programming?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Dynamic programming and state design. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Elements left unchanged must form a nondecreasing subsequence. The longest such subsequence has length 4, for example 2,3,4,6 at indices 1,3,5,7.
2. A DP with d[i]=1+max d[j] over j<i and A[j]≤A[i] gives lengths [1,2,2,1,3,2,4], proving there is no longer one.
3. Keep 2,3,4,6 and replace the other three elements to obtain [2,2,3,3,4,4,6]. Minimum replacements=7−4=**3**.

#### GATE 2026 CS2 · Q39 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/dynamic-programming?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Dynamic programming and state design. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Every T[i][j] depends only on T[i−1][j] and T[i][j−1]. Row-major B1 has completed the prior row and current row’s preceding column, so it respects both dependencies.
2. In B2, both predecessors have coordinate sum s−1 and were completed in the previous diagonal iteration, so it also respects dependencies.
3. Both are correct: **A**. Their costs differ: B1 is Θ(n²), while the written triple-loop B2 is Θ(n³) despite only Θ(n²) updates.
